rows.name: small Mario (player) — 2x4 OAM metasprite box, visible 16x16 in the lower half
rows.notes:
Proof: list_sprites in the first screen of World 1-1 (game_mode $0770=1, small Mario standing on the left hill). Player y $00CE read 176, so the metasprite box top is OAM y=177. The game lays the player out as a 2-wide x 4-tall (16x32) OAM box; for small Mario the top two rows are blank $FC filler and only the bottom 16x16 carries his pixels. Every entry uses sprite palette 4. Entries, as (screen x, screen y) CHR tile, and offset from the box top-left (40,177), with flip:
- (40,177) CHR $FC — blank filler, offset (0,0), no flip
- (48,177) CHR $FC — blank filler, offset (8,0), no flip
- (40,185) CHR $FC — blank filler, offset (0,8), no flip
- (48,185) CHR $FC — blank filler, offset (8,8), no flip
- (40,193) CHR $3A (OAM tile 58) — visible top-left, offset (0,16), no flip
- (48,193) CHR $37 (OAM tile 55) — visible top-right, offset (8,16), no flip
- (40,201) CHR $4F (OAM tile 79) — visible bottom-left, offset (0,24), no flip
- (48,201) CHR $4F (OAM tile 79) — visible bottom-right, offset (8,24), h-flipped
The paired $4F tiles are the two shoes/feet (the right one mirrored); $3A/$37 are the cap+face half and the mirrored half. OAM slots rotate every frame, so identify Mario by position + these tiles.
rows.why: OAM $3A/$37 over $4F/$4F(h) under four $FC fillers, palette 4, sprite table $0000; rendered from sprite CHR they are small Mario standing, as drawn at (40,193)

rows.name: small_mario_sprite_palette (red cap/shirt, orange skin, olive-brown hair/shoes)
rows.notes: Sprite palette 4 = [$22, $16, $27, $18] in PPU RAM. What each slot paints on small Mario: slot 0 $22 periwinkle is never drawn (sprite pixel value 0 is transparent); slot 1 $16 red paints his cap and shirt (the large red areas); slot 2 $27 orange paints his face/skin and hands; slot 3 $18 olive-brown paints his hair, mustache and shoes (the dark detail). Proof (World 1-1, paused): baseline get_pixel_color(45,204) on the cap/shirt read $16 red, get_pixel_color(44,196) on the face read $27 orange. write_palette(4,1) $16 -> $2C cyan and step_frame 1: the cap and shirt turned cyan (get_pixel_color(45,204) = $2C cyan) while the face pixel (44,196) stayed $27 orange — so slot 1 is exactly the red cap/shirt, not the skin. clear_palette_overrides restored slot 1 and get_pixel_color(45,204) read $16 red again. Only Mario uses this palette on this screen (the Goomba is palette 7), so the change recoloured Mario alone.
rows.why: after slot 1 was written $2C, Mario's cap and body are cyan in this screenshot (rgb 72,205,222 in his box) and face/hair are unchanged; slot 1 cap/body, 2 skin, 3 linework/hair/shoes as claimed

rows.name: Status bar HUD layout (MARIO/score, coin, WORLD, TIME)
rows.notes: Fixed status bar drawn on nametable 0, BACKGROUND PATTERN TABLE $1000 (so nametable tile $xx draws CHR $1xx), attribute palette 2 (white $30 text on the shared $22 sky). Proven twice with read_nametable 0 rows 0-3 plus a screenshot: (1) in World 1-1 (game_mode $0770=1 at CPU $0770, scroll_x 0, paused) and (2) on the title screen after reset_emulator ($0770=0). Screen pixel = (col*8, row*8). ROWS 0-1 (screen y 0-15): every column $24 = blank sky. ROW 2 (y 16-23) = the labels: cols 3-7 'MARIO' = tiles $16 $0A $1B $12 $18; cols 18-22 'WORLD' = $20 $18 $1B $15 $0D; cols 25-28 'TIME' = $1D $12 $16 $0E. ROW 3 (y 24-31) = the numbers: cols 3-8 = the 6-digit score (read $00 x6 = 000000, directly under MARIO); col 11 = coin icon $2E (attribute palette 3 = orange), col 12 = 'x' $29, cols 13-14 = 2-digit coin count (read $00 $00); cols 19-21 = world/level '1-1' = $01 $28 $01 ($01 = digit 1, $28 = hyphen); cols 26-28 = 3-digit TIME (in 1-1 read $03 $04 $08 = '348', matching the screenshot; on the title screen those three cells read $24 blank because the timer is not running). The same glyph tiles are also the game's font elsewhere (e.g. the title screen '1 PLAYER GAME' menu and the copyright line), so tile ids name one picture each: record keyed by chr id (table 1).
rows.why: against the screenshot: MARIO cols 3-7, WORLD cols 18-22 with W $20, TIME cols 25-28 on row 2; score cols 3-8, coin icon background $2E at col 11 (palette 3), x $29 col 12, coins 13-14, 1-1 cols 19-21, TIME 26-28 on row 3; all right
